steps.title: What is Wingspan?
steps.content:
You're bird enthusiasts — researchers, bird watchers, and collectors — seeking to discover and attract the best birds to your wildlife preserves. Each bird you play has a real species, real habitat, and special powers!

**Goal:** Score the most points over **4 rounds** by playing bird cards, laying eggs, collecting food, and achieving bonus objectives.

steps.title: What's on the Table
steps.content:
- **Your player mat** - Has 3 habitat rows: Forest, Grassland, Wetland (each with 5 slots for birds)
- **Bird cards** - 170 unique birds with food costs, habitats, nest types, egg capacity, point values, and powers
- **Food dice** (in the birdfeeder dice tower) - 5 custom dice showing food types
- **Miniature eggs** - Used for laying eggs and as a resource
- **Food tokens** - Invertebrate, Seed, Fish, Fruit, Rodent (+ wild)
- **Bonus cards** - End-of-game scoring goals
- **Round-end goal tiles** - Competitive objectives each round
- **Bird tray** - 3 face-up bird cards available to draw

steps.title: Setting Up
steps.content:
1. Each player takes a **player mat** and **8 action cubes** of their color
2. Shuffle bird cards, deal **5 to each player** and place 3 face-up in the bird tray
3. Deal each player **2 bonus cards** — keep 1, discard the other
4. Give each player **5 food tokens** (1 of each type)
5. Now **choose:** you start with 5 birds and 5 food, but must discard down. For each bird you keep, discard 1 food. (Keep 3 birds + 2 food? Or 2 birds + 3 food? Your choice!)
6. Place a **round-end goal tile** for each of the 4 rounds
7. Roll all 5 **food dice** into the birdfeeder

steps.title: What Happens on Your Turn
steps.content:
On your turn, place **one action cube** on your player mat to do one of these 4 actions:

**1. Play a Bird** (top of any row) - Pay its food cost and egg cost, place it in the matching habitat row

**2. Gain Food** (Forest row) - Take food dice from the birdfeeder. Activate Forest bird powers left-to-right.

**3. Lay Eggs** (Grassland row) - Place eggs on your birds (up to their egg limit). Activate Grassland bird powers.

**4. Draw Bird Cards** (Wetland row) - Draw from the tray or deck. Activate Wetland bird powers.

**Key insight:** As you add birds to a row, that action gets **stronger** because you activate all birds in the row!

steps.title: Playing Birds & Bird Powers
steps.content:
**To play a bird:**
1. Choose a bird from your hand
2. Check its **habitat** icon — it can only go in that row (some birds fit multiple habitats)
3. Pay the **food cost** shown on the bird card (discard food tokens)
4. If it's not in the leftmost column, also pay an **egg cost** (1 egg for columns 2-3, 2 eggs for columns 4-5)
5. Place the bird in the leftmost empty space in the correct row

**Bird Powers** (3 types):
- **When Played** (brown) — Happens once, when you first play the bird
- **When Activated** (pink) — Happens every time you use that row's action
- **Once Between Turns** (teal) — Can trigger on other players' turns

steps.title: Rounds & Scoring
steps.content:
The game lasts **4 rounds**. Each round you have:
- Round 1: **8 turns** (8 action cubes)
- Round 2: **7 turns** (1 cube goes to round-end goal)
- Round 3: **6 turns**
- Round 4: **5 turns**

**At round end:** Score the round-end goal (e.g., "most birds in Wetland"). Place one action cube on the goal board.

**Final scoring adds up:**
- Points printed on your bird cards
- Bonus card points
- Round-end goal points
- 1 point per egg on your birds
- 1 point per food cached on birds
- 1 point per tucked card

steps.title: Let's Play Your First Turn
steps.content:
Look at your starting birds and food. Here's a good first-turn plan:

1. **Look at your bird cards' food costs.** Do you have the right food to play any of them?
2. If yes: **Play a bird!** Put it in the matching habitat. You'll have powers to activate on future turns.
3. If no: **Gain food** from the birdfeeder. Pick dice showing the food you need.

**Early strategy tips:**
- Play birds early — they make your actions more powerful as the game goes on
- Forest birds help you gain more food
- Grassland birds help you lay more eggs (needed to play birds in later columns)
- Wetland birds help you draw more bird cards

Don't worry about memorizing everything — the player mat guides you through each action step by step!
